correctness.rationale: Theorem 2.3 of arXiv:2610.04179v1 supplies bounded continuous semiconjugacies \(H=\operatorname{Id}+h\) and \(K=\operatorname{Id}+k\). In \(\mathbb R^n\), bounded displacement makes each map proper. For each target \(y\), the homotopy \(x\mapsto x+t h(x)-y\) is nonzero on a sufficiently large sphere, so Brouwer degree remains \(1\) and forces a preimage; similarly for \(K\). Proper surjective semiconjugacies pull compact forward-invariant sets back to compact forward-invariant sets, and compact-space entropy monotonicity gives both inequalities for \(h_{\mathrm{cpt}}\).

value.rationale: The source deliberately stops at non-surjective semiconjugacies in its general Banach theorem. In finite dimension, bounded displacement removes surjectivity as an obstruction and yields genuine mutual factor maps. This transports compact invariant subsystems through proper preimages and forces exact equality of a natural noncompact entropy invariant while leaving the harder injectivity and conjugacy problem untouched.
